title: Convert Hourly to Annual Pay with Salary Sacrifice to Superannuation
description: Learn how to convert hourly rate to annual salary for a 38-hour week, including casual loading, super paid on top, and salary sacrifice to superannuation. Use our calculator.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top and casual loading added separately.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of your base hourly rate, compensating for lack of paid leave. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading. Your annual pay is then calculated as $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80 before tax and super. Super is paid on the ordinary earnings (base rate or loaded rate depending on award), but always on top of your gross pay.

faqs.q: What is salary sacrifice to superannuation and how does it affect my take-home pay?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice to superannuation is an arrangement where you ask your employer to contribute some of your pre-tax salary into your super fund instead of paying it to you as cash. This reduces your taxable income, so you pay less tax. However, it does not reduce the super guarantee (which is paid on top of your salary). The sacrificed amount is still subject to super guarantee, but it counts towards the concessional contributions cap. Our calculator does not deduct salary sacrifice, but you can estimate the tax saving by reducing your taxable income by the sacrificed amount.

faqs.q: How is super guarantee calculated on my pay?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. Ordinary earnings generally include your base hourly rate (or loaded rate for casuals) for all hours worked, but not overtime. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830 per year. If your annual ordinary earnings exceed that, super is only paid on the first $270,830. For example, on a $33.05 per hour casual rate working 38 hours a week, annual ordinary earnings are $65,306.80, so super is $65,306.80 × 12% = $7,836.82 paid into your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: The 38-Hour Week

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the standard way to compare them is to convert your hourly pay to an annual figure. In Australia, the typical full-time week is 38 hours, so the formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a 38-hour week, that’s **hourly rate × 38 × 52**. This assumes you work every week of the year at the same rate, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It’s a useful benchmark, but your actual pay may differ.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For example, if your weekly pay is $1,004.90 (the National Minimum Wage for 38 hours), your fortnightly gross is $2,009.80. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that quote a fortnightly figure.

## Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

Australia has a [National Minimum Wage](/topics/minimum-wage) set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. This is the legal floor for most employees not covered by an award or agreement.

However, many workers are covered by **award rates** that set higher minimums for specific industries or roles. These rates are also per hour and may include allowances. Always check your award or enterprise agreement – the Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award.

If you are a **casual employee**, you are entitled to a **casual loading** of 25% on top of your base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our [timesheet](/), you can enter your base hourly rate and check the box to add 25% casual loading. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator adds it for you.

## Super Guarantee: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay **super guarantee** into your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the rate is **12% of your ordinary earnings**, paid **on top of your gross pay**. This means your total employment cost is higher than your salary. For example, on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for 38 hours:

- Weekly ordinary earnings: $1,004.90
- Super guarantee: $1,004.90 × 12% = $120.59
- Total cost to employer: $1,125.49 per week

The super guarantee has a **maximum contribution base** of **$270,830 per year** (2026–27). If your annual ordinary earnings exceed that, super is only paid on the first $270,830.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) withholds tax based on the **2026–27 resident tax rates**:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on the next $26,800 (up to $45,000)
- 30% on the next $90,000 (up to $135,000)
- 37% on the next $55,000 (up to $190,000)
- 45% on anything above $190,000

Plus, the **Medicare levy** is generally **2%** of your taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide.

To estimate your [take-home pay](/topics/take-home), subtract tax and Medicare from your gross pay. Remember, super is not deducted from your pay – it is an extra contribution by your employer.

## Salary Sacrifice to Superannuation

One way to reduce your taxable income is through **salary sacrifice to superannuation**. This is an arrangement where you ask your employer to contribute some of your pre-tax salary into your super fund instead of paying it to you as cash. The sacrificed amount is taxed at only 15% (within the concessional contributions cap), which is often lower than your marginal tax rate.

For example, if you earn $80,000 per year and salary sacrifice $10,000 to super, your taxable income drops to $70,000. You save the difference between your marginal tax rate (30% plus 2% Medicare) and the 15% super tax. However, salary sacrifice does not reduce the super guarantee – your employer still pays 12% on your ordinary earnings (which includes the sacrificed amount).

Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide explains more. Note that our calculator does not deduct salary sacrifice – it shows gross pay before any such arrangement. You can manually adjust your taxable income to estimate the effect.

## Comparing with Averages

The [Australian Bureau of Statistics](/topics/average-pay) (ABS) reports **Average Weekly Earnings** for May 2026:

- Full-time adult ordinary time: **$2,083.70 per week**
- All employees total earnings (including part-time): **$1,579.20 per week**

These are **averages**, not medians for any specific job. Your pay may be higher or lower depending on your industry, experience, and location. For job-specific pay data, refer to [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/), the home page, lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates:

- Weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay
- Super guarantee (12% on ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base)
- Estimated tax and Medicare levy
- Estimated take-home pay

Remember the disclaimer: this is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

## Key Takeaways

- **Annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52** for a standard full-time week.
- **Casual loading** is 25% on top of the base rate – use the checkbox on our timesheet.
- **Super guarantee** is 12% paid on top of ordinary earnings, up to the cap.
- **Salary sacrifice to superannuation** can lower your taxable income, but does not affect the super guarantee calculation.
- Always check your award or agreement for your correct minimum rate. The National Minimum Wage is the floor, but many awards pay more.
